claim: Heterochromatin is enriched for specific epigenetic factors including Heterochromatin Protein 1a (HP1a).
source: Heterochromatin is enriched for specific epigenetic factors including Heterochromatin Protein 1a (HP1a), and is essential for many organismal functions.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about heterochromatin composition.

claim: Heterochromatin is essential for many organismal functions.
source: Heterochromatin is enriched for specific epigenetic factors including Heterochromatin Protein 1a (HP1a), and is essential for many organismal functions.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction regarding pericentromeric sister chromatid cohesion, chromosome pairing and segregation, and genome integrity.

claim: The study purified Drosophila melanogaster HP1a interactors.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach taken in the study, described in the abstract and detailed in the methods.

claim: The study performed a genome-wide RNAi screen to identify genes that impact HP1a levels or localization.

evidence: This is a direct statement of the experimental approach, with detailed methodology provided in the manuscript.

claim: Over four hundred putative HP1a interactors and regulators were identified, the majority of which were previously unknown.
source: The majority of the over four hundred putative HP1a interactors and regulators identified were previously unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Table 1 and supplementary materials showing 135 HPips from IP-MS and 374 HPprs from RNAi screen.

claim: 13 of 16 tested candidates (83%) are required for gene silencing.
source: We found that 13 of 16 tested candidates (83%) are required for gene silencing, providing a substantial increase in the number of identified components that impact heterochromatin properties.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 4 showing PEV assay results.

claim: Although some HP1a interactors and regulators are broadly distributed within the heterochromatin domain, most localize to discrete subdomains.

evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data in Figures 5, 6, 7 and Table 3 showing different localization patterns.

claim: HP1a interactors and regulators display dynamic localization patterns during the cell cycle.

claim: A network of subdomains regulates diverse heterochromatin functions.

evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time-lapse imaging observations.

claim: Some ADD1 signal remains attached to chromosomes during mitosis, even though most ADD1 and all detectable HP1a are removed.
source: Interestingly, even though most ADD1 and all detectable HP1a are removed during mitosis, some ADD1 signal remains attached to chromosomes, distinguishing it from all other HPips analyzed here.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time-lapse imaging observations.

claim: FK506-bp1 displays a narrow localization pattern as well as a ring around the nucleolus throughout much of the cell cycle.
source: Another striking example is FK506-bp1, which displays a narrow localization pattern as well as a ring around the nucleolus throughout much of the cell cycle
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 4 and Video 5.

claim: FK506-bp1 accumulates foci outside of heterochromatin during G2.
source: Interestingly, FK506-bp1 accumulates foci outside of heterochromatin during G2, which do not colocalize with markers for replication (PCNA), centromeres (CID) or telomeres (HOAP) (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time-lapse imaging observations.

claim: Lhr displayed its previously described localization pattern (broad and centromeric).
source: Supporting the validity of our approach, Lhr displayed its previously described localization pattern (Brideau et al., 2006) (broad and centromeric; Table 3, Figure 7—figure supplement 5 and Video 6).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section with a supporting citation and imaging data.

claim: XNP exhibits narrow and focal localization patterns in S2 cells.
source: However, in contrast to a previous report that XNP/ATRX is broadly enriched at polytene chromocenters (Bassett et al., 2008), we observe that XNP exhibits narrow and focal localization patterns in S2 cells
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 6 and Video 7.

claim: Some Lhr and XNP foci colocalize within the same nucleus, while others do not.
source: Emphasizing the complexity of subdomain architecture, we detected some Lhr and XNP foci that colocalize within the same nucleus, while others do not (Figure 7—figure supplement 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 5C.

claim: The localization patterns for 5 of the 7 HPips studied with time-lapse imaging are dynamic throughout the cell cycle.
source: We conclude that the localization patterns for 5 of the 7 HPips studied with time-lapse imaging are dynamic throughout the cell cycle
evidence: This is stated in the Results section based on time-lapse imaging data.

claim: The complementary approaches utilized in this study enabled identification of different classes of heterochromatin proteins.
source: This hypothesis is supported by studies demonstrating that loss of HPips does not cause visible defects in HP1a domain organization (e.g. SMC5/6 [Chiolo et al., 2011], KDM4A [Colmenares et al., unpublished]). Therefore, we propose that the complementary approaches utilized in this study enabled identification of different classes of heterochromatin proteins.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the Discussion section based on the different types of hits identified by each approach.

claim: The RNAi screen enriched for hits upstream of HP1a deposition, while the IP-MS enriched for genes acting downstream of HP1a loading onto chromatin.
source: A potential reason for poor overlap is that the RNAi screen enriched for hits upstream of HP1a deposition, while the IP-MS enriched for genes acting downstream of HP1a loading onto chromatin.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the Discussion section to explain the lack of overlap between the two screens.

claim: Broadly distributed proteins could encode structural components important for universal aspects of heterochromatin architecture and function.
source: We speculate that broadly distributed proteins could encode structural components important for universal aspects of heterochromatin architecture and function (e.g. nucleosomal ordering, variable accessibility of exogenous proteins, and coalescence of heterochromatin domains; reviewed in [Elgin and Reuter, 2013]).
evidence: This is speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Subdomains may regulate specific functions or localized, dynamic structural changes.
source: In contrast, subdomains may regulate specific functions or localized, dynamic structural changes (e.g. decreased compaction to enable transcription, histone exchange).
evidence: This is speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Heterochromatin may be just as structurally and functionally dynamic and diverse as euchromatin.
source: Heterochromatin may be just as structurally and functionally dynamic and diverse as euchromatin, and increased understanding of its organization will likely yield important insights into the nuclear architecture and genome biology.
evidence: This is speculation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Many HP1a binding partners contain a conserved PxVxL-like motif.
source: Previous studies showed that many but not all HP1a binding partners contain a conserved PxVxL-like motif
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with reference to previous studies.

claim: HP1a can oligomerize at least up to tetramers.
source: HP1a can oligomerize at least up to tetramers (Wang et al., 2000; Zhao et al., 2000; Canzio et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.

claim: HP1a oligomerization forms a multivalent platform for HPip binding.
source: HP1a can oligomerize at least up to tetramers (Wang et al., 2000; Zhao et al., 2000; Canzio et al., 2011), forming a multivalent platform for HPip binding (i.e. more than one HPip binding site per HP1a oligomer).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section as part of a proposed model.

claim: HP2 and PIWI have higher binding affinities for HP1a proteins containing phospho-mimic mutations in the HP1a chromo shadow domain.
source: Consistent with the PTM model, HP2 and PIWI have been shown to have higher binding affinities for HP1a proteins containing phospho-mimic mutations in the HP1a chromo shadow domain (Mendez et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with a supporting citation.

claim: HP1a is extensively post-translationally modified by SUMOylation, acetylation, methylation, formylation, ubiquitination and poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation.
source: HP1a and its orthologs are extensively post-translationally modified by SUMOylation, acetylation, methylation, formylation, ubiquitination and poly(ADP-ribosyl)ation (Alekseyenko et al., 2014; Lomberk et al., 2006; LeRoy et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion section with supporting citations.
